str.label: Strength
str.title: Strength Guide
str.blurb: What every point of Strength does in Fallout 76 — carry weight and melee damage, worked out live from the game files — and every way to boost it.
str.intro: Strength is your raw physical power. It decides how much you can carry and how hard your melee attacks hit. High Strength does not add damage to guns or heavy weapons directly, but it lets you equip more of the Strength perk cards that do.
details: Strength starts at 1 and caps at 100 points (actor value limits).
Melee mods that add fire, energy, cryo, poison or electrical damage scale with Strength and Melee Damage buffs.
Heavy weapons: Strength does not raise heavy weapon damage on its own — it buys room for the Strength heavy weapon perk cards.

dr.blurb: How Damage Resistance (DR) cuts physical damage in Fallout 76 — the real formula from the game files — and every way to raise it.
dr.intro: Damage Resistance reduces physical damage — bullets, blades, fists and claws. It works on a curve: every extra point is worth a little less, and the bigger the hit, the less your DR stops.
details: For most enemies 300–400 DR is plenty. Expeditions, raids, nuked bosses, Encryptid and Daily Ops usually need 700+ together with damage reduction perks and gear.
Past roughly 350 resistance you get diminishing returns — damage reduction (not resistance) is the better next step.

formulas.label: Damage taken after resistance
formulas.expr: 100 * clamp(pow(dmg * factor / max(res, 1), exp), 1 - maxred, 1 - minred)
formulas.note: Damage taken = hit × (hit × factor ÷ resistance) ^ exponent, kept between the game's minimum and maximum reduction. Bigger hits get through more.

details: Each point of Disease Resistance takes 1% off your chance of catching a disease (SURV_ScaleDiseaseChance perk on the player).

Iron Stomach, Natural Resistance and Thirst Quencher only work while you are free of disease.
Disease Resistance food buffs are not boosted by diet mutations or Strange In Numbers.

overview.title: SPECIALs & Stats Overview
overview.blurb: What SPECIALs and stats are, how buffs stack, which stats each build should buff — and a link to the full guide for every SPECIAL and stat.
overview.credit: Thank you to Gilpo, Mapex and Zeek for their patience and for answering my constant questions.

sections.title: SPECIALs and Stats
sections.html:
SPECIALs are your character's core abilities — Strength, Perception, Endurance, Charisma, Intelligence, Agility and Luck. Each one feeds a set of stats: carry weight, health, Action Points, V.A.T.S. hit chance, XP and more.

Stats decide how well you fight, explore and survive. These guides show what every point does — worked out live from the game files — and every way to buff it, so you can decide what is worth chasing for your build.

sections.title: Tips, Tricks and Information
sections.html:
Food buffs

Most food buffs of the same type do not stack — two Intelligence foods will not raise Intelligence twice; the newest one replaces the first. AP Refill is the exception: those stack.

Stack these on top of food

  • Alcohol
  • Ally buffs
  • Armour effects and mods
  • Bobbleheads
  • Chems
  • CAMP buff stations
  • Event buffs (e.g. Path to Enlightenment)
  • Magazines
  • Mutations
  • Perk cards

Damaged limbs

  • Crippled head: distorted vision and slower healing.
  • Crippled arms: harder to aim.
  • Crippled torso: slower AP regen.
  • Crippled legs: slower movement.

Hunger and thirst

Empty hunger and thirst bars no longer hurt you, but full ones still give you bonuses. Run the Rejuvenated perk card and Perfect Bubblegum with your food buffs for extra stats — see the Hunger & Thirst Bar Explained guide.

sections.title: Recommended Buffs for Your Build
sections.html: Pick a build and commit to it — min-max and hybrid builds work, but they cost a lot to keep buffed. These are the bare-minimum stats to buff for each kind of build; the Recommended Food Buff Calculator picks the actual food, chems and drinks for you.
